data.name: Mimic Hunter
data.detailed_description:
Mimic Hunter is an innovative, gameplay-wise 2.5D, hardcore platform game that will take you on an epic adventure as the legendary master hunter Monsieur Ratimousse embarks on a journey to find his old mentor Barnabas and stop an ancient demonic force from devouring the mortal world. Unsheathe your sword and your platforming skills to climb forsaken towers, fight nefarious Mimics, solve unforgiving puzzles in an attempt to uncover the grim truth behind the nature of the Unbound. En garde!



Mimic Hunter was initially created as an entry for GameJolt's Adventure Jam 2017 #AdvJam2017 in no more than 2 weeks by Aliza Wenders and Derwen Llewelyn from Angry Cat Studios. But the journey doesn't end there! In those two weeks, we grew to love this game even more than we'd have anticipated, and we decided to tell this uncommon story in its full length, with all the gore and glory! During the early development, we succeeded in creating a very unique, stable and innovative platforming experience, but we had to cut a megaton of features and ideas (and most of the story content) due to the lack of time. And that simply couldn't stand! Now the whole story is ready, and it's awaiting a hero: You! ;-)



A free demo of the original #AdvJam2017 version is available on GameJolt, check it out! Just don't forget: it's only a fragment of what's to come!



  • Unique, cylindrical, mind-bending environment
  • Hand-drawn, macabre-esque art style and animations
  • Lore-rich story with many surprises, twists and mysteries across 7 unique levels (at least 5 hours of playtime even for pro Mimic Hunters!)
  • Hardcore platforming gameplay with traps, timed puzzles and more!
  • Fencing! En garde!
  • Dangerous and mischievous, various enemy types, each with its unique behavior
  • A fully-fledged Tower Builder with which you can create and share your own adventure!
  • Special game modes: Time Attack and Survival
  • Fully remappable control scheme (with partial controller support)
  • Steam achievements

What is the goal of the game?

The story mode takes you on an adventure to defeat a mysterious ancient force that threatens the mortal world. During your journey, you will encounter nefarious enemies, unravel the secrets of the Hunters' Guild's past, and solve demonic riddles and puzzles.

How long the main story is?

As Mimic Hunter is designed to be quite a hard game with scenarios that take multiple attempts to figure out and solve, we can only estimate the actual game time you'll need to complete the story featuring seven unique towers. On average, it takes a player about 5-10 hours to finish the main story, depending on player skill and chosen difficulty level.

What are the key gameplay elements?

Mimic Hunter is primarily a platformer, thus jumping, climbing and fighting are very important to master. Additionally, there are riddles and puzzles you can't solve by platforming only: you'll need to collect lore and figure out the secrets. Fencing is also very important to overcome your foes, and you must learn how to do it properly. You'll be also able to handle a lot of situations by avoiding combat or defeating your enemies via the environment if you're cunning enough.


How in-depth the Tower Builder is?

The Tower Builder (a.k.a. level editor) you get is identical to the one we used to create the majority of the content. You can create any kind of tower with dialogues, scripted puzzles, traps, events, and share it with other people! Basic editing is quite intuitive, but a full documentation/manual is also available.

Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Win 7 / 8.1 / 10 (32-bit)
  • Processador: "3rd generation" Intel Celeron 2 GHz or equivalent
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: nVidia GeForce 400 series / AMD Radeon 6000 series or better
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0c
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 1 GB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: Any DirectX compatible
  • Notas adicionais: Keyboard and mouse required

reviews.review:
[quote][b]This review was written for [url=http://store.steampowered.com/curator/31837076/] My Curation Page. [/url] [/b]
[i]I received a reviewing copy of this game for free. However, my review is honest.[/i] [/quote]

I received this game via Steam Curator Connect. Thanks!

[i]Skip to the bottom for my Final Thoughts[/i]

Mimic Hunter is a 2.5D action platformer by Angry Cat Studios, originally developed during a Gamejolt game jam. Unfortunately Mimic Hunter is plagued by worse than awful controls that completely ruin gameplay.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
The graphics in Mimic Hunter are decent to say the least. The graphics are by no means a Van Gogh or even an artists rendition of a Van Gogh but that's not to say the graphics are awful. There is a certain charm to them and I like the 2.5D revolving tower that the game takes place in. The setting is very macabre and dark although I don't completely understand why the enemies are mimics (chests that are actually just monsters). That being said the graphics fit the setting but are mediocre in general.

[h1]Audio & Soundtrack[/h1]
The music in Mimic Hunter is decent as well but not bad either. The music fits the theme of the game really well and helps set the mood although the sound effects could use some polishing. The main menu music is also subpar however I did not spend too much time on the title screen.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The gameplay. Oh god the gameplay. The controls almost made me delete the game after just 15 minutes of playtime. It took me a little over 20 minutes for me to even figure out most of the controls in the tutorial. For a game that relies heavily on platforming as one of its key gameplay elements you would have thought that the developers would have perfected their jumping but the game is a complete opposite. I haven't even talked about the hitboxes yet. The hitboxes are completely broken (I was able to push an enemy that was under me and the enemy was able to attack me through the stone slab I was standing on). If an enemy attacks you while you are under a stone step then you are essentially paralyzed and you can only attack. If 2 or more enemies attack you when you're pinned like that then you might as well be dead. 

Note I played this with a keyboard and mouse. The other reviews claim that the game is a lot more enjoyable with a controller however I do not own a controller that I can plug into my computer.

[h1]Storyline[/h1]
The story in Mimic Hunter is a bit confusing. Although I do appreciate the developers efforts to actually have a story (which a suprising amount of games I've reviewed do not), I feel as if they tried too hard to cram in all the exposition. The first level had what felt like ages of dialog boxes that could have been easily avoided if there was voice acting which would have made the storyline aspect of the game 1000x better.

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
Overall Mimic Hunter is what should be a pretty decent game but is completely ruined by unresponsive and crappy controls, broken hitboxes and mediocre graphics. Avoid this game until the developer fixes these issues.

Rating:
Graphics: 5.5/10
Audio: 6.0/10
Gameplay: 1.3/10
Storyline: 6.5/10
Overall: 4.8/10

reviews.developer_response:
Hey,

Thank you for your detailed feedback! We're sorry you didn't find the gameplay and controls good enough, probably it's a different cake.

We certainly carefully and thoroughly tested the whole campaign experience, with emphasis on jumping (as it is a platformer), and found everything in good shape (as it can be seen in any of the videos here, and in many others on our YouTube channel and Twitter as well), so there's nothing "to fix" about jumping or controls per se (as can bee seen in other users' video reviews), but we value your feedback and will try to change things regarding other issues if other players' opinions should align with yours. Mimic Hunter is not a speedrunner, it's a puzzle-platformer where you have to carefully time and execute your actions.

Again, thank you for taking the time to review the game.

Kind regards,
Angry Cat Studios
